extra_quotes: A four-channel wavelength division multiplexing implementation achieves 92.25% accuracy on a four-class Fashion-MNIST task and an estimated throughput of 115.2 GOPS over 144 m of computing fiber.
An architecture-level projection indicates an intrinsic throughput density of 1.6 POPS m−1 for eight wavelength channels operating at 100 Gbaud per wavelength.
The maximum reduction in forward optical power is approximately 20%, corresponding to an insertion loss of 0.97 dB

This value represents an ideal scaling estimate, whereas the practically achievable throughput density will also be constrained by the FBG fabrication pitch and precision, transmitter and receiver bandwidths, accumulated optical loss, available dynamic range, chromatic dispersion, and inter-channel crosstalk.
